notes: Read discovery, diamond, fees and ranking public-policy role files and reviewed merged implications for all 14 records. This skeptical review supplies 14 complete field replacements (route, difficulty, metrics, review, formats and scope_notes) and 14 findings. Source role files are unchanged.

Coverage: live official author/fee policies were independently retrieved for 13 venues and attempted for JEPP. JEPP direct instructions remained blocked; official indexed publisher text was used with its weaker access status preserved. Sage’s current submission/page/publication charge list was inspected end-to-end; the four disputed titles are absent. Journal-specific explicit no-fee statements are the affirmative basis of their restored standard routes, corroborated by the list, rather than silence alone.

Eligibility after review: 10 verified_free, 3 needs_verification (Policy Sciences, Science and Public Policy, JEPP), 1 conditional (Cambridge Journal of Public Policy). The four Sage restorations do not assert a free overlength allowance or erase optional colour/OA/service costs.

Metric coverage: independently reproduced four Sage acceptance values (PPA 7.3%, AAS 17.1%, Evaluation 23.4%, ARPA 7.5%), Sage’s all-final-decisions/previous-calendar-year definition, the dated Policy Sciences and OUP citation/usage evidence, official indexed JEPP metrics, and Cambridge’s historical 2024 article counts. STH 9.2% and PWMP 21.6% remain ranking-role official-page observations; this reviewer obtained their page metadata but repeated body fetches timed out. This limitation is explicit in their audit notes rather than reported as an independently reproduced value.

Acceptance metric year 2025 for Sage/JEPP is derived from the publisher-defined previous full calendar year at the 2026-11-16 check, not a year printed beside each rate. Citation metric years 2025 and Cambridge publication-count year 2024 are printed explicitly. Undated Cambridge/JDD citation metrics and period-ambiguous speed displays remain excluded.

Difficulty is a provisional agent judgment within the relevant specialty, never an acceptance probability or a cross-discipline prestige ranking. Policy Sciences and Internet Policy Review were changed from high to unknown because detailed fit/desk standards alone did not establish comparative selectivity. JDD’s qualitative high judgment retains the explicit selective-review/limited-capacity basis and its absence of an official acceptance rate.

IPR: independently read its current author page, September 2026 AI policy and desk criteria; retained both the webpage prohibition on AI article authorship and the detailed permitted/disclosed uses. Research screening delay and op-ed closure are separate. JDD format inconsistencies, CJLG edited-section exceptions and Policy Quarterly speech exceptions remain visible.

No venue was contacted, no manuscript submitted, and no account, membership or paid service purchased. Independent agent review is policy verification, not human scientific review, manuscript acceptance assurance or a guarantee against later policy changes.
